canonical_views.label: Neighbourhood orbit
acceptance_criteria: The subject plot can be identified within five seconds.
Approximately ten surrounding streets read as one continuous neighbourhood.
Roads, source-derived footprints, land cover and water remain spatially coherent.
No floating buildings, broken surfaces, stretched imagery or empty horizon is visible.

canonical_views.label: Street approach
acceptance_criteria: The default camera reads at credible human eye height.
The route, plot relationship and nearby building scale are understandable.
Orbit, pan and zoom remain usable without opening evidence panels accidentally.
Vegetation and detail support rather than obscure the source-bound context.

canonical_views.label: Plot and terrain
acceptance_criteria: The plot boundary is continuously draped across the display terrain.
The oblique default camera makes relative fall legible rather than flattening the land.
The plot remains unmistakable without implying a legal or surveyed boundary.
Labels, warnings and evidence controls do not cover the primary subject.

canonical_views.label: Architectural concept hero
acceptance_criteria: The selected preview fills enough of the frame to read as architecture rather than a box.
Roof, façade, entrance, glazing and terrace expression are visibly legible.
The house-to-plot, terrain, sun and view relationships can be understood.
The design remains explicitly concept and unselected until the user acts.

canonical_views.label: Three-scheme comparison
acceptance_criteria: All three schemes use the same plot, camera and display terrain basis.
The three architectural strategies are recognisably different without relying on labels.
Roof form, footprint, volume count and design signals are visible and comparable.
No scheme is ranked, approved or selected without explicit user action.
